customer: So I'm selling my hatchback before I head back to campus, and I got an offer online, which is great, but my roommate said the price can drop once someone actually looks at it in person? I only have one key because the spare disappeared sometime last semester, and also I've probably driven a few hundred miles since I filled out the form because of all the trips home to Eastvale. Will that mess things up, and what happens if I don't like the new number?
agent: Thanks for reaching out! As explained in our article "What can change your offer at the appraisal," the appraisal confirms your offer unless we find something your online answers didn't mention, and a missing key or remote takes $150 off for each missing key. Mileage only becomes a reason for a lower offer if it's more than 300 miles above what you entered, along with things like unreported damage, warning lights, or aftermarket parts that need to be removed or replaced. The specialist will show you the reason for any change before you decide, and you can always say no and keep your car.
